public_rationale: Accuracy was a real commercialization barrier: BCG found it the leading reported obstacle in information services. Deloitte also documented limited movement from experiments into production, alongside several other barriers. But adoption and reported benefits were increasing. These findings support a narrower claim that unreliability impeded some deployments. They do not establish that it principally explains halting commercial progress across generative AI, nor does growing adoption disprove that explanation.
limitations: Survey responses identify perceived barriers rather than isolating causal effects.
The evidence is concentrated in enterprise use and does not cover every commercial market.
A weaker reading requiring only some reliability-related delays would receive stronger support.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Commercial progress of generative AI has been halting because the technology is not reliable.

statement.excerpt: Commercial progress has been halting precisely because the tech simply isn’t reliable.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that unreliable generative-AI outputs materially impeded commercialization, with reliability a principal explanation for uneven progress.
Halting does not mean that adoption or commercial successes were absent.
The surrounding two-year retrospective supplies an approximate observation window of 2022-11-28 through 2024-11-28.
Enterprise deployment studies can test part of this claim, but one industry's experience cannot establish the cause of commercial progress across the whole market.
criteria.support_condition: Broad deployment evidence shows substantial commercial delays or stalled deployments and identifies output unreliability as a principal cause.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence shows broadly unhindered commercialization, or establishes that reliability was immaterial to the observed delays and other factors explain them.

evidence.explanation: BCG surveyed 100 information-services professionals in early 2024 and found accuracy the leading reported barrier. This directly supports the proposed mechanism within that sector, without establishing its importance across the entire generative-AI market.

evidence.excerpt: much more likely now than in 2023
evidence.publisher: McKinsey & Company; report hosted by ABBYY
evidence.explanation: The survey conducted February 22–March 5 reported regular organizational generative-AI use at 65%, nearly double its earlier survey. This is material counterevidence to a broad stagnation reading, but increased use does not establish that commercialization proceeded without reliability-related delays.

evidence.locator: Opening description of survey; findings under the subsequent deployment, risk, and experimentation sections
evidence.explanation: In this May–June survey, 68% reported moving no more than 30% of experiments into production, while 67% were increasing investment because of value already obtained. Compliance, risk management, governance and data problems featured among the barriers; the report does not isolate factual unreliability as their principal cause.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative historical deployment evidence linking substantial delays or cancellations to output unreliability, with comparisons against other causes and a clear measure of commercial progress.
